newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: France offers S.Africa help against fish poaching.
newsitem.headline: France offers S.Africa help against fish poaching.

text.p: France on Tuesday offered to help South Africa combat high-seas poachers who are ravaging stocks of the valuable Patagonian toothfish in their Antarctic breeding grounds.
"There is a real and terrible danger for both our countries," French ambassador Tristan d'Albis told a briefing aboard the French navy frigate Ventose, moored in Cape Town harbour.
"We are prepared to share with South Africa our research, our information, our techniques," he said.
"We are prepared to send a mission from Paris to give more details. I hope you (South Africa) will be interested in it because we are both in the same boat," d'Albis said.

The toothfish, named for the South American waters where it was first discovered, has in recent years been found in other parts of the southern oceans for which South Africa and France, among other countries, have treaty responsibilities.

South African sea fisheries official Rudi Laan, who attended the French briefing, said it was estimated that poachers had taken toothfish worth about 350 million rand ($80 million) from the seas south of South Africa over the last year.
"This must be damaging the stocks. We are very concerned," Laan said. He said South Africa had secret plans to combat the poachers.
The Ventose is one of several French warships based at Reunion which patrol the southern Indian Ocean, with a mandate to open fire on fish poachers if necessary.

South Africa's military chiefs have frequently complained that they do not have enough navy ships to protect fish stocks. Parliament is expected to approve later this year the purchase of four corvettes.
D'Albis said toothfish fetched around $7.0 a kilogram in Japan and the United States.
He said poaching in the southern oceans had reached such a level that toothfish stocks could be largely wiped out within two years.
